why: Commit 2 is a decision read from production figures (which model families already cache by themselves) and from the provider's current API reference for the cache marker through the AI Gateway, which the brief forbids writing from memory and hands to a stronger executor. make_it_cheaper: Split the step: commit 1 alone with the exact new managerPrompt() tail and toolsNow() code written in the brief is cheap-then-review; commit 2 waits for the measured shares and a written marker form, after which it too is specified.
brief_problems: Commit 2 and stop_if 2 and 5 carry '[an executor]' placeholders instead of saying which model does the work.

Commit 1 leaves the agent-eval replay test failing on main until a person records the eval; with the full checks reporting beside the deploy that is accepted, but any later push with a migration (which waits for every check) is blocked until the recording lands.
